# skycloak_cluster_features (Resource)

Manages the full set of customer-managed enabled Keycloak feature flags on a cluster. Use one resource per cluster. Removing a flag turns it off. Destroy clears all customer-managed enabled flags. Skycloak-managed flags are preserved. Changes restart Keycloak. The API key needs the `clusters:read` and `clusters:write` scopes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "skycloak_cluster_features" "example" {
  cluster_id = skycloak_cluster.example.id
  features   = ["cimd"]

  # Use the maintenance window by default.
  # Set apply_now = true to restart immediately and wait for Keycloak.
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster ID. Immutable.
- `features` (Set of String) Complete set of enabled flags. Use an empty set to turn them all off. See the `skycloak_cluster_features` data source for the catalog and version requirements.

### Optional

- `apply_now` (Boolean) Set to `true` to restart immediately, including for changes already pending. Defaults to `false`, which schedules changes for the maintenance window when one is enabled. Without an enabled window, changes apply immediately. Terraform waits for immediate restarts to finish. This setting also controls the restart on destroy and defaults to `false` on import.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite ID `cluster_id/features`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import skycloak_cluster_features.example 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
```
